case_studies.title: Agents-K1: Towards Agent-native Knowledge Orchestration
case_studies.abstract: Current LLM-based research agents have advanced through agent orchestration, yet largely overlook scientific knowledge orchestration. Existing works often reduce papers to abstracts, surface mentions, and flat \texttt{cites} edges, omitting key entities, claims, evidence, mechanisms, and method lineages essential for scientific reasoning. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of efficiently converting raw scientific documents into useful knowledge graphs, the authors built a pipeline called Agents-K1, and the result is an end-to-end knowledge orchestration system. Agents-K1 helps to preserve key entities, claims, and evidence from scientific papers. It's not directly related to cloud infrastructure management.

case_studies.title: Toward Secure LLM Agents: Threat Surfaces, Attacks, Defenses, and Evaluation
case_studies.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are rapidly moving from conversational interfaces to software components that plan, invoke tools, maintain memory, and act on external environments. This transition changes the nature of security risk. In agentic settings, failures are no longer limited to unsafe text generation. Untrusted content may redirect control flow, misuse tool privileges, corrupt persistent state, leak sensitive information, or trigger harmful external actions. At the same time, research on LLM agent security is expanding quickly but remains fragmented across attack families, defense
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of security risks in large language model agents, building a framework to identify and mitigate threats, and resulting in a better understanding of potential attacks and defenses. The study focuses on the transition of LLMs from conversational interfaces to software components that interact with external environments. The research aims to address the expanded security risks in these new settings.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage cloud infrastructure that uses large language models, here is what to do: review your current security measures, assess potential attack surfaces, and consider implementing additional defenses to mitigate risks. This flags a risk: if your organization uses LLM agents, check for untrusted content and tool privileges immediately. Check your current LLM deployments for any signs of security breaches or vulnerabilities.

case_studies.title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning from Delayed Marketplace Feedback for Objective-Weight Adaptation in Three-Sided Dispatch
case_studies.abstract: Dispatch in three-sided marketplaces provides a natural setting for reinforcement learning from world feedback: decisions are evaluated by delayed operational outcomes such as delivery speed, courier utilization, and merchant congestion. We present a deployed reinforcement learning system at DoorDash that adapts dispatch objective weights in a large-scale food-delivery marketplace using delayed signals. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of optimizing dispatch in three-sided marketplaces by adapting objective weights using delayed marketplace feedback. The researchers built a reinforcement learning system that learns from logged marketplace data to shift the dispatch optimizer's trade-offs. The result is a deployed system at DoorDash that improves dispatch decisions in a large-scale food-delivery marketplace.

case_studies.title: Learning What to Remember: Observability-Safe Memory Retention via Constrained Optimization for Long-Horizon Language Agents
case_studies.abstract: Long-horizon language agents accumulate observations, reasoning traces, and retrieved facts that exceed their finite context windows, making memory retention a fundamental resource-allocation problem. Existing memory systems improve management through heuristic scoring, retrieval optimization, or learned compression, but largely treat retention as a local decision problem and do not explicitly model its long-term consequences under realistic observability constraints. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of memory retention in long-horizon language agents by building a constrained optimization model, resulting in more efficient memory usage. The model allows agents to retain relevant information while discarding unnecessary data. This research is not directly relevant to IT infrastructure work.

case_studies.title: MiniMax Sparse Attention
case_studies.abstract: Ultra-long-context capability is becoming indispensable for frontier LLMs: agentic workflows, repository-scale code reasoning, and persistent memory all require the model to jointly attend over hundreds of thousands to millions of tokens, yet the quadratic cost of softmax attention makes this untenable at deployment scale. We introduce MiniMax Sparse Attention (MSA), a blockwise sparse attention built upon Grouped Query Attention (GQA). case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of quadratic cost of softmax attention in large language models by introducing MiniMax Sparse Attention, which enables sparse retrieval and reduces costs. The researchers built a blockwise sparse attention mechanism called MiniMax Sparse Attention. The result is a more efficient attention mechanism for large language models.

case_studies.title: TAHOE: Text-to-SQL with Automated Hint Optimization from Experience
case_studies.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have democratized database access through Text-to-SQL, but moving from prototypes to production remains difficult. Real deployments must handle strict SQL dialects, massive schemas, and evolving user preferences, while supervised fine-tuning is costly and rigid and agentic test-time scaling is expensive. We present Tahoe, a system that treats prompt optimization as a dynamic data management problem. case_studies.summary: The research solves the problem of making Text-to-SQL systems more reliable and efficient in real-world deployments by creating a system called TAHOE that optimizes SQL queries. TAHOE uses a dynamic data management approach to learn from errors and user interactions. The result is a more robust and adaptable Text-to-SQL system.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage databases or deploy Text-to-SQL systems, consider evaluating TAHOE to improve query optimization and reduce errors. case_studies.title: Knowing When to Ask: Self-Gated Clarification for Hierarchical Language Agents
case_studies.abstract: In hierarchical reasoning, failures often originate at intermediate decision points where the agent commits to a wrong branch without recognizing that it lacks critical information. Rather than treating clarification as an external uncertainty trigger, we propose ACTION-RATING, a formulation that places it inside the agent's action space on a shared ordinal scale with navigation, so that asking competes directly with acting at every decision point and help-seeking becomes observable at intermediate states. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of language agents making incorrect decisions due to lack of information by introducing a self-gated clarification mechanism. The researchers built an agent called ACTION-RATING that can ask for clarification at any decision point. The result is that the agent can now recognize when it lacks critical information and seek help, leading to more accurate decisions.

case_studies.title: TimeLens: On-Device Artifact Recognition with Retrieval-Augmented Question Answering for the Grand Egyptian Museum
case_studies.abstract: TimeLens is an AI-powered bilingual mobile guide for the Grand Egyptian Museum (GEM). Pointing a phone at an exhibit, a visitor sees the artifact recognized in real time and can ask follow-up questions answered in English or Arabic. The work addresses three problems specific to in-gallery deployment: fine-grained visual similarity among 51 catalogued artifacts (many near-identical Ramesside statues), the gap between curated training data and handheld camera conditions, and the risk of an AI guide stating unsupported historical facts. Two engineering contributions are reported. First, an on-dev
case_studies.summary: TimeLens solves the problem of recognizing and providing information about artifacts in a museum setting by building an AI-powered mobile guide that can identify exhibits and answer visitor questions in real-time. The researchers built a retrieval-augmented question answering system that can handle similar-looking artifacts and varying camera conditions. The result is a reliable and accurate mobile guide for the Grand Egyptian Museum.

case_studies.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have enabled time series (TS) analysis by jointly modeling numerical observations and textual context through a shared token interface. case_studies.title: Influcoder: Distilling Decoders' Gradient Influence Rankings into an Encoder for Data Attribution
case_studies.abstract: With the growth of LLMs' (Large Language Models) capabilities, there has been an increasing push to curate high quality datasets by filtering samples in the training data. In general, Data Attribution (DA) methods aim to estimate how individual samples in a training dataset can precondition a model to generate certain outputs. As an example, one might be interested in which samples in the data could be the source of toxic behavior after training the LLM. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of identifying which data samples in a training dataset influence the outputs of Large Language Models, the authors built a tool called Influcoder, and the result is a method to attribute data samples to specific model outputs. This could help improve data quality by filtering out unwanted samples. The research is focused on machine learning model training data quality.

case_studies.title: Operads for compositional reasoning in LLMs

In this paper, we propose operads, mathematical structures that model many-in, one-out operations and compositions thereof, as a natural framework for describing question decomposition. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of improving large language models' reasoning by breaking complex queries into simpler sub-queries. The authors built a mathematical framework using operads to describe question decomposition. The result is a more rigorous approach to question decomposition in large language models.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work, as it focuses on improving large language models' reasoning capabilities, which is more relevant to AI and machine learning development.

case_studies.title: One Polluted Page Is Enough: Evaluating Web Content Pollution in Generative Recommenders
case_studies.abstract: Search-augmented LLMs increasingly mediate everyday consumer recommendations by retrieving live web content. This creates a new risk: generative recommenders may consume polluted web content, such as fake reviews and promotional pages crafted to mislead recommendations. We ask: to what extent do search-augmented LLMs become unwitting promoters of fake products when consuming polluted retrieval results? case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of generative recommenders promoting fake products due to polluted web content, by introducing a benchmark called FORGE to measure fake-product promotion, and found that even one polluted page can affect recommendations. The researchers built FORGE to evaluate web content pollution in generative recommenders and found significant risks. The result shows that search-augmented LLMs can become promoters of fake products when consuming polluted retrieval results.
